title: 6. Elucidating the role of the CXCL12/CXCR4 chemokine axis in regulating vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) localization during sheep pregnancy.
content:
Abstract
Successful pregnancy outcomes are vital for livestock productivity, yet embryonic loss and fetal morbidity remain major constraints to reproductive efficiency and economic return. Proper vascularization during implantation and placentation is essential for pregnancy success and is regulated by various angiogenic factors. Of these, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is the most potent driver of angiogenesis at the fetal–maternal interface throughout gestation. Improved understanding of VEGF regulation may reveal strategies to enhance pregnancy outcomes through targeted vascular development. Activation of the CXCL12/CXCR4 chemokine axis stimulates VEGF expression and in turn VEGF increases expression of both CXCL12 and CXCR4 in other biological systems, making this pathway a promising target for modulation of VEGF-mediated angiogenesis during gestation. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of manipulating CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling during implantation on VEGF expression at the fetal-maternal interface across gestation in sheep. Pregnant Rambouillet ewes received continuous intrauterine infusion via osmotic pump beginning d12 of gestation of saline (CON), AMD3100 (CXCR4 antagonist; 1X, 1.5X, or 3X), or CXCL12 ligand (Lo12 or Hi12) to inhibit or activate the CXCL12/CXCR4 axis, respectively. Treatments were delivered for up to 14 days, depending on study. Uterine and placental tissues were collected during early-gestation (d20), mid-gestation (d90) and near term (d135). All tissues were fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde, paraffin-embedded, and mounted for immunofluorescent detection of VEGF. Images were collected at a standardized exposure and analyzed using quantitative image analysis with background correction and defined regions of interest for each ewe. Immunofluorescent signal intensity was analyzed using parametric or nonparametric models, depending on data distribution, with treatment considered the main effect. On d20 of gestation, inhibiting CXCR4 with AMD3100 at both 1.5X and 3X treatments significantly reduced VEGF immunoreactivity (P < 0.01) compared to controls. Additionally, Hi12 ewes also exhibited reduced VEGF localization (P < 0.01), while Lo12 ewes were similar to CON ewes. Immunoreactivity for VEGF was primarily observed in trophoblasts and luminal (LE) and glandular epithelium (GE). In both d90 and d135 placentomes, there were no significant differences in VEGF immunoreactivity and localization between 1X, 1.5X, and 3X treated ewes compared to CON ewes. At these later stages of gestation, VEGF localization was concentrated around chorionic villus vasculature, including endothelial cells, trophoblast, and stromal compartments. These findings indicate that early gestational CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling influences VEGF-associated angiogenic activity during implantation but has a limited detectable impact on VEGF localization after mid-gestation. This axis may be a key upstream regulator of VEGF-mediated angiogenesis during implantation and may lead to novel treatments for influencing livestock pregnancy success through improved fetal-maternal vascularization.
